title: Forms Used After '{il faut que}' and '{je veux que}'
description: Learn verb forms that appear after '{il faut que...}' and '{je veux que...}' phrases. sois (be), ait (have), aille (go), fasse (do). Essential for telling people what you want them to do!
can_do: Use special verb forms for wishes and necessities
Form the foundation for subjunctive expressions
Prepare to express complex ideas at B2 level

concepts.definition: French uses different verb forms after phrases like '{il faut que}' (someone needs to), '{je veux que}' (I want someone to), '{je suis content que}' (I'm happy that someone...). These express wishes, needs, or emotions about OTHER PEOPLE's actions.
concepts.example: Normal statement: {Tu es sage} (You are good). Wish about you: {Il faut que tu sois sage} (You need to be good - different form!)

concepts.term: Where You CAN Use These Forms
concepts.definition: ONLY after certain phrases: il faut que, je veux que, je suis content que, j'ai peur que, avant que, pour que, bien que, etc.
concepts.example: ✓ {Il faut que tu sois sage} (You need to be good), ✓ {Je veux qu'il aille} (I want him to go)

concepts.term: Where You CANNOT Use These Forms
concepts.definition: DON'T use these for normal statements, questions, or with just il faut/je veux (no '{que}')
concepts.example: ✗ {Tu sois content?} (Wrong! Say: {Tu es content?}). ✗ {Il faut aller} (Correct - no '{que}' = normal form)

concepts.definition: If you see '{que}' + a person after these starter phrases, use these forms!
concepts.example: {il faut QUE tu} → use sois/{aies}/{ailles}/{fasses, je veux QUE tu} → use sois/aies/ailles/{fasses}
